sections.h2: Where is Delaware County, Indiana, and what is its landscape?
sections.html:
Delaware County is in east central Indiana, with Muncie as both the county seat and the largest city, about 50 miles northeast of Indianapolis. The county covers 395.91 square miles, with 392.12 of them land.

The land is low rolling prairie with fertile soil. The Mississinewa River flows west through the north, and the White River runs west through the center and past Muncie. Prairie Creek Reservoir, southeast of Muncie, is managed by the city. The highest ground is a hilly area in the southeast corner. Blackford, Jay, Randolph, Henry, Madison and Grant counties surround it.

Muncie sits on the West Fork of the White River at 935 feet. Its climate is humid continental, with about 40 inches of precipitation and 25 inches of snow in a typical year, which matters to roofs, gutters and furnaces on older houses.

Delaware County was authorized in 1820 and organized in 1827 on land gained through the 1818 Treaty of St. Mary's. It takes its name from the Delaware people, who settled along the White River and were moved west of the Mississippi in the 1840s.

Muncie began as a trading post renamed Muncietown and was platted as the county seat in 1827. The name was shortened in 1845, the town incorporated in 1854 and it became a city in 1865.

The natural gas boom changed everything. Indiana's first natural gas well opened in 1884, and the Ball brothers brought a glass foundry to Muncie in 1888. Iron and steel mills followed, and Kitselman Steel and Wire was the largest employer in Indiana in 1900 with 11,000 workers.

sections.h2: What does the Delaware County economy rely on now?
sections.html:
The Delaware County economy has shifted from manufacturing toward education, health care and retail. The Ball family donated the school property that became the forerunner of Ball State University, which opened in 1918, and helped fund Ball Memorial Hospital, which opened in 1929.

  • Ball State University: 3,379 employees in 2022
  • IU Health Ball Memorial Hospital: 2,613
  • Muncie Community Schools: 650
  • Navient: 633
  • Magna Powertrain: 571

Ball Corporation closed its Muncie glass facilities in 1962 and moved its headquarters to Colorado in 1998. Newer manufacturers include Brevini Wind, which arrived in 2009, and Progress Rail, a Caterpillar subsidiary, which arrived in 2011. Growth has concentrated on the north side of Muncie, while the older industrial south side has seen less.

Residents disagree about how to read that change. Older workers tend to identify with manufacturing, while newer residents focus on education and health services. Muncie also drew national attention as the subject of the Lynds' 1929 Middletown study, and Ball State's Center for Middletown Studies continues that research.

Delaware County is run by a seven-member county council and a three-member board of commissioners, and it has five circuit courts. It lies in Indiana's 5th congressional district and is part of the Muncie metropolitan area, within the larger Indianapolis, Carmel and Muncie combined statistical area.

Muncie spreads across Center, Hamilton, Harrison, Liberty and Mount Pleasant townships. The county Assessor's Office keeps property cards with some transfer history and maintains legal descriptions for parcels in Center Township. About 76.9% of county residents live in urban areas, and the median age countywide is 36.7.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit affect Delaware County homes?
sections.html:
Interstate 69 runs just west of Muncie, and U.S. Route 35 plus State Routes 3, 32, 67 and 332 also serve the city. The Cardinal Greenway rail trail runs 60 miles from Richmond to Marion through the area.

Muncie Indiana Transit System operates 14 fixed bus routes, daily except Sundays. Delaware County Regional Airport has no commercial service, and the nearest commercial airports in Fort Wayne and Indianapolis are each about 75 miles away.

sections.h2: When are Delaware County property taxes due, and where do I pay?
sections.html:
Delaware County property taxes are due on or before May 10 and November 10, and the county says the date moves if it lands on a weekend or holiday. The state's 2026 calendar listed May 11 and November 10.

The Auditor's office is at 100 West Main Street, Room 103, Muncie, IN 47305, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The phone number is 765-747-7717. The Treasurer's mailing address on file is 100 W Main St, Room 102. We could not confirm the Treasurer's current hours or payment methods on an official page, so call before you go.

  • To change the mailing address on your tax statement, go to the Auditor's office.
  • If statements are not coming in your name, contact the Plat Room at the same number.
  • Mortgage deductions need signatures, so visit the Auditor in person. A reverse mortgage can qualify with a lender statement showing the debt.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Delaware County assessment?
sections.html:
Indiana's Form 130 deadline is June 15 of the year the county mails the assessment notice, or of the year the tax bill goes out when no notice is sent. You file one petition for each parcel with the assessing official.

The assessor then holds an informal meeting and reports back to the Property Tax Assessment Board of Appeals. State guidance requires the hearing within 180 days of filing, with notice mailed at least 30 days ahead. If you disagree with the result, Form 131 goes to the Indiana Board of Tax Review. We did not find a Delaware County assessor page with current deadlines, so confirm with the county.

A homestead deduction can matter as much to a final bill as a lower assessed value. Under the statute we reviewed, the standard deduction is 60% of assessed value up to $48,000 for assessment dates after 2022, with a January 5 filing date. It was amended effective January 1, 2025, so verify the current rule.

sections.h2: What happens with a Delaware County tax sale and surplus?
sections.html:
When a Delaware County property is sold at a tax sale, only the owner whose property was sold can claim the surplus. Anyone else, even with a power of attorney, must petition the court.

The surplus becomes available only after the court issues a tax deed and the deed is recorded with the Delaware County Recorder's Office. Questions go to the Auditor's office at 765-747-7717.

Before that, the late penalty is 5% of the delinquent tax when paid within 30 days and no earlier delinquency exists, or 10% in other cases. Selling the house before a tax sale can avoid losing it to a certificate holder.

sections.h2: What do Delaware County sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Delaware County sellers often have older houses, inherited property or rental units. The sales disclosure form is required before a deed reaches the auditor, and each parcel needs its own form.

  • Get a payoff figure for taxes and any penalties.
  • Confirm the mailing address on the tax bill.
  • Gather estate papers if the owner has died.
  • Decide whether repairs make sense before selling.

Cash buyers can close without a lender appraisal, and the title company settles taxes from your proceeds.

faqs.q: When are Delaware County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due on or before May 10 and November 10 each year, and the date shifts when it falls on a weekend or holiday. The state's 2026 calendar listed May 11 and November 10.

faqs.q: Where do I change the mailing address on my Delaware County tax bill?
faqs.a: Make the request at the Auditor's office, 100 West Main Street, Room 103, Muncie. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. and the phone is 765-747-7717.

faqs.q: Who can claim surplus from a Delaware County tax sale?
faqs.a: Only the owner whose property was sold. Anyone else must petition the court, even with a power of attorney. Surplus is available after a tax deed is issued and recorded.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Delaware County assessment?
faqs.a: The state deadline is June 15 of the year the notice or tax bill is mailed, on Form 130. File one petition per parcel and check your notice for the exact date.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Delaware County house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid taxes and penalties are paid from your proceeds at closing, and a cash sale can close before a tax sale happens.
